## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

RaceDao — core-data/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/data/db/RaceDao.kt

## Trigger

persist, called after writing a race — from RaceRepositoryImpl.saveImportedRace, saveRecordedRace and replaceReference — observed

## Today

RaceDao.upsert is `@Transaction`-scoped over the delete-then-insert of
the race row and its children only, and returns the resulting raceId.
RaceRepositoryImpl.persist then makes a second, separate DAO call,
`raceDao.findById(raceId)!!`, outside that transaction, to read the
row back. A delete executing between the two calls (upsert's
transaction has already committed by then) leaves findById returning
null, and the `!!` crashes instead of failing gracefully.

## Expected

The write and the read-back happen inside one transaction: RaceDao
carries a single `@Transaction`-annotated method that performs the
delete/insert and the `findById` query in the same transactional body
and returns the resulting RaceEntity (or null if the row is gone)
directly, rather than handing back only an id for a second, unguarded
call. RaceRepositoryImpl.persist no longer force-unwraps a
separately-fetched row; when the row is gone it surfaces a failure
(§13 — a repository returns a result type, never crashes on a race it
cannot help). This changes persist's return shape from a bare `Race`
to something that can carry absence, which in turn means
RaceRepositoryImpl.replaceReference — which currently calls
`persist(race.copy(isReference = true))` and discards the outcome,
always returning `Result.success(Unit)` — must observe that outcome
and propagate a failure instead of unconditionally succeeding.

## Searched

persist, findById(raceId)!!, upsert, @Transaction, RaceDao
